Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Can CTE difference alone determine warpage sign?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Layer order, thickness, modulus, cure history, and reference temperature also matter.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R7: IEEE TCPMT, Thermomechanical Challenges of 2.5-D Packaging | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10256204

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Layers with different coefficients of thermal expansion and stiffness cannot expand freely when bonded; bending can result. Trace the visual in order: CTE mismatch; bonded layers; curvature. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Sketch silicon on an organic substrate as temperature changes. Identify which layer tends to expand more; do not infer curvature sign without the actual stack and stress-free state.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R7: IEEE TCPMT, Thermomechanical Challenges of 2.5-D Packaging | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10256204
R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Global warpage can signal risk, but joint fatigue depends on local displacement, geometry, material behavior, and cycling. Trace the visual in order: global shape; joint location; local strain. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Mark an outer-corner bump and a central bump in a package sketch. Predict which sees a larger relative displacement under one idealized thermal cycle, then name missing data.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
